title: Funerals, tombs and the second line
summary: Describes playing sad music to the vault, then 'Didn't He Ramble' and the second line afterward, including Crip, who led on his peg leg.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: It's a funny thing, when we used to play, like, play funerals, you know, and play a funeral -- that's a real kick. We played funerals and get to the grave,

the graveyard, and they buried most of the people in New Orleans in vaults, like in tombs, you know, because it's like swampland still, you know. They can't bury so deep because it's muddy and the soft mud and all that. So they make -- they called vaults, you know, and they play all this sad music going to the grave and they stand around when they put the character -- whoever died -- in the vault -- tomb, they call it, and seal him up. And the band turned around and come out and they say, "Ta-tat," and then the second line get together and all of a sudden they start out with "Didn't He Ramble" and, boy, then they start. Then they carry on and they dance all through the street, and at the second line, that's when the fun starts. Then everybody starts.

All those youngsters and even the crippled characters -- there was a guy called "Crip". He had one leg. He would be the leader sometimes, leading the second line on his peg leg. So it was a lot of fun.
